fixes.explanation: That's right. "The LORD brings this charge against the elders and leaders of His people…" (Isaiah 3:14). Nothing here is hidden. The charge goes straight to the ones in charge.

That's right, friend. No kings from other nations are mentioned. God says, "I will make mere lads their leaders, and children will rule over them." (Isaiah 3:4). The replacements are lads and children.
Rubble is the word. The man says, "Take charge of this heap of rubble." (Isaiah 3:6). Think about that job posting for a second. Come on in, we've got a heap of rubble, and the job is YOURS!

He actually says no, and loudly. The man cries aloud, "I am not a healer. I have no food or clothing in my house. Do not make me leader of the people!" (Isaiah 3:7). His brother just got seized him into a leadership job and he is NOT having it.

Walls are a fair guess, friend, but they're never brought up. Isaiah says, "…Jerusalem has stumbled and Judah has fallen because they spoke and acted against the LORD…" (Isaiah 3:8). The cause the verse gives is how they spoke and acted toward the LORD. Walls aren't mentioned.

That's right. Isaiah says, "…like Sodom they flaunt their sin; they do not conceal it." (Isaiah 3:9). Sodom was a city known for its sin (Genesis 19). There's no hiding going on here at all, because it's out in the open.

Running away is what a lot of us would expect, but the verse doesn't say that. The message is, "Tell the righteous it will be well with them…" (Isaiah 3:10). What the righteous are told is that it will be well. Fleeing isn't part of the message.

Yes, and it's God Himself saying it. "O My people, your guides mislead you; they turn you from your paths." (Isaiah 3:12). The ones meant to point the way are steering people off course. I think that's a heavy thing to hear, and He still calls them "My people."

Temple is a guess I understand, friend. But the LORD says, "the plunder of the poor is in your houses." (Isaiah 3:14). What they're holding is the poor's plunder. The temple isn't part of this charge.
